name: Every Concept of a Geometrically Realizable Ample Family Is a Peeling Endpoint
statement: If an ample family is the chamber-sign family of finitely many affine hyperplanes on a nonempty open convex polyhedron, then it corner-peels to every prescribed concept. Consequently no rooted factor is geometrically realizable. Geometric realizability is inherited by coordinate faces, so any family having a rooted factor as a coordinate face is nonrealizable; in particular the remote opposite-status families are all nonrealizable, including their ordinarily peelable sides.
proof: Choose a point in the prescribed chamber and first bound the realizing polyhedron without changing its sign system. A generic affine functional close to a hyperplane separating that chamber from another chamber defines a moving halfspace that keeps the chosen point. At the first nontrivial sweep event, the Knauer--Marc corner sweep deletes one COM corner; in a lopsided system this is one ordinary corner, and the remainder is again an ample geometric realization containing the chosen point. Iteration peels to the prescribed chamber. Coordinate-face inheritance follows by intersecting with the fixed open sign halfspaces and forgetting their hyperplanes.
